items.text: EA SPORTS FC 27 version 1.2.0 is now live and includes the updates below.
Adjusted how defenders position themselves with extreme defensive line heights.
Defenders will now drop off sooner while still maintaining a higher line than other tactics.
This will be released as a Live Tuning Update alongside the Title Update.
Improved some cases of fullbacks dropping too deep while defending.

To reduce the effectiveness of scoring after a kick off, the defensive line will not drop back as far into the penalty box directly after a kick off and a defensive player will be lined up more centrally.
Improved some cases of AI teammates drifting offside.
Slight improvements to Attacking AI inside the box during certain counter attacks situations.
Increased the impact of the Defending Aggression CPU Slider.
In Street Football, improved the goalkeepers ability to save low driven shots.
After a header pass, player control did not switch to the pass receiver.
Fixed an issue where your teammate would not go after a loose ball following a missed shot.
Fixed an issue where your teammate would not go after a loose ball following a slide tackle.
Teammates could sometimes stop their run after a pass is made while waiting for it to be completed.
In Street Football 1v1s, the goalkeeper could sometimes leave the net when the ball was shot at the opposite side of the pitch.
Input delay could have impacted corner kick aiming indicators during online matches.
Defenders could be out of position after a deep free kick.
In rare cases, when performing a seal out, players could be temporarily frozen in place.

The attribute boost from Amps were incorrect.

[p align="start"]In our previous Developer Notes for The Grounds, we shared that we were actively investigating incorrect Attribute Point (AP) costs for certain upgrades. Now that we’ve had a chance to evaluate a couple weeks of live gameplay, we want to share an update on where things stand and outline the next steps we are taking.

[p align="start"]When we designed the Player Archetypes system as part of FC 27, our goal was to create progression routes that allowed players to build their Pros with distinct differences in both Attributes and PlayStyles to fit their unique tactical preferences.

[p align="start"]With the live data that we now have following the worldwide launch of the game, we are adjusting Attribute Point costs to better align the system with our intended design for Archetype identity.
[p align="start"]To help balance these cost adjustments, we are removing Attacking Positioning as a requirement for Archetype Specializations, granting you more flexibility to allocate your AP.

[p align="start"]Because of the coupled changes to upgrade costs and requirements, we’ve made the decision to reset Attribute Points for Archetypes in an update that will be deployed by Thursday, October 22th, 2:00am Pacific Time.

[p align="start"]It’s important to note, your level and total amount of AP you have per Archetype will not change. However, you will need to redistribute your AP across your Attributes following the update.

[p align="start"]We realise this means you will need to spend additional time calculating and setting up your Pros again. To support your transition to the updated system, any Player who has previously created a Pro (and will therefore need to reallocate their Attribute Points) will receive 5,000 Club Coins and one 1.75x AXP Multiplier for 6 Matches.
[p align="start"]Our goal is to preserve the balance of the game, accentuate Archetype identity, and deliver the player experience we had in mind when we built these features.

[p align="start"]As part of our investigation, we found that certain Attributes were being classified incorrectly, which impacted their AP costs. We are correcting these costs while also making targeted changes to better align progression with each Archetype’s identity.
[p align="start"]While we want to minimize disruptions to your progression, making this adjustment early in the season ensures we will have a stable and balanced foundation for the year ahead.
[p align="start"]Here is a preview of the updated Attribute Points system:

Acceleration

GK Positioning
GK Reflexes

items.text: It’s been great to see players jump into The Grounds, meet other players, and spend time across the different in-world activities. So far, we’re seeing plenty of activity around small-sided football, including 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, and In-World Rush.

The early data is also highlighting some clear areas where we can improve. One of the biggest is Kickabouts. While small-sided football has been incredibly popular, that popularity has also made it harder for players to find enough people to start matches in some of the other activities around The Grounds.
What We’re Hearing From You
We’ve been monitoring your feedback closely, and there are a few topics that have come through particularly strongly.
Winner Stays and Win Streaks

We’ve seen a lot of requests for a way for winners to stay on a pitch and build a streak. We’re already seeing players and streamers track their own streaks and create some fun competition around them, and we think there’s an opportunity to better support that directly in The Grounds.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/060950283d2a3f094065facfdca23fd917ee5080.png"]WIP image
We’ve already begun exploring potential designs for this experience. We’ll share more details as our investigations lead to more concrete plans for updates to the game.
Kickabout Matchmaking and Queueing
When players get a Kickabout going, we’re hearing that the experience can be a lot of fun. The challenge right now is getting enough players together to start one.

We know this can make some activities much harder to jump into than we want them to be, and there isn’t one single change that solves the problem. We’re looking at a few different approaches, including ways for players to signal that they need more people at a particular gameplay site, ways to connect players across servers while keeping them in the world experience, and scheduled Kickabout-focused events that could bring more players into these activities at the same time.
Long-term Fatigue in Clubs 11v11

We heard the feedback that infinite stamina could disproportionately benefit Clubs with more players compared to smaller Clubs. Based on this feedback, we’ve reintroduced long-term fatigue in Clubs in Title Update v1.0.1, and will be watching closely over the coming days to understand how the change feels in practice.
Menu Performance
Many of you have told us that menus within The Grounds can sometimes feel slow to load or unresponsive. We’re actively tracking this and continuing to look into where we can improve the experience.
Other Quality-of-Life & Live Issues
We’re continuing to address issues as they are identified, investigated, and ready to release. Some current examples include:
5-star skill moves not working in small-sided matches: A fix has been deployed.
High ping in some cross-region Clubs matches: A fix has been deployed.
Incorrect Archetype Point costs for certain upgrades: We are investigating.
1v1 goalkeepers behaving erratically: We are investigating.
Teleport access to Stadium and Clubhouse portals: We are testing a potential fix.
11v11 drop-in position preferred position not being applied correctly: We are testing a potential fix.
Unable to open the world map while queued: We are testing a potential fix.
Map input opening the Season Pass: We are testing a potential fix.
This is only the beginning for The Grounds. We’re continuing to watch the data, listen to your feedback, and make improvements as more players spend time in the mode.

Keep telling us what’s working, what isn’t, and what you’d like to see next. We’ll also be hosting a Grounds & Clubs specific Q&A in the Official EA SPORTS FC Discord, stay tuned for an official date and time announcement. You can also continue to share your FC 27 feedback through the Player Feedback Portal..

Welcome to our first FUT Developer Notes for FC 27.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/94ac278809c402e69214a09ef02de1c06ba820ac.png"]
It’s been great to see you building your squads, trying out the new ways to play and progress, and sharing plenty of feedback along the way.

With the first few days of FC 27 behind us, we wanted to talk a little more about what we’re seeing across Ultimate Team, some of the conversations we’re following closely, and what the team is already working on.
Gameplay is also an important part of the Ultimate Team experience, so make sure to take a read of the recent Gameplay Developer Notes.

It’s been exciting for us to see how players are taking to The Gallery. We’re seeing players share strategies, find creative ways to complete Set Grades, and chase the Hall of FUT players they want most.

It’s been especially encouraging to see Gallery give more Player Items a reason to matter, even when they aren’t going straight into your squad. We’ll continue to add new Sets and refresh the Token Store, and we’re excited to see how your Galleries develop from here.

That change is already having an impact. Coin balances are more than 10% higher than at the same point last year. We’re also seeing plenty of activity on the Transfer Market, with more Starting XI players being picked up from the Market.
It’s an encouraging early sign that having more flexibility is giving you more choice in how you build and improve your team.

Beyond the Transfer Market, we noticed many players are spending time with the new PvE Live Events. So far, they’re the third most played FUT experience behind Rivals and Squad Battles. We know having more ways to play matters, and we’ll continue building on Live Events as the year progresses.

Finally, more than 150,000 players have already linked their EA Account with partner sites like FUT.GG, FUTBIN and FUTWIZ. We’ve loved seeing what those sites are already building with the data, and we’re looking forward to giving them more to work with over time.
One of the biggest conversations we’re following right now is around Evolutions and the broader pace of squad progression.
We know how important Evos are for keeping the players you care about in your team.
We’re looking at all the different ways you can improve your squad, whether its Evolutions, SBCs, mode rewards and Campaigns, to make sure they feel balanced alongside one another.
We’ll keep listening as squads develop and make sure the different paths to improving your team continue to feel worthwhile.

Streamlined SBCs have also been a big part of the early conversation. We’re hearing that many players appreciate being able to complete SBCs with less friction. We’re also seeing useful quality-of-life suggestions, like better ways to mark or favourite the players you want to keep. Keep those suggestions coming, this is a feature we expect to keep improving.

We also know the balance between rewards earned across FUT and what appears in the Store matters a lot. This year, we’ve taken a more focused approach to Store offers, with fewer offers, and changes to how those offers are structured.
That same thinking carries into Campaigns, where we’re taking a more focused approach with smaller Campaign squads.

We’re also watching how the increased end-of-match rewards feel over time, particularly as players reach daily limits and weekly milestones. The goal is simple, even after you’ve reached a major reward threshold, playing another match should still feel like it moves your Club forward.
On 28 September, we brought Streamlined SBCs to the Companion App, making it easier to complete and manage SBCs when you’re away from your console or PC.
We know how much of your squad management happens away from the console or PC, so having Streamlined SBCs available on the Companion App should make completing and managing SBCs much easier.
Now that it’s in your hands, we’ll keep building on it with more quality-of-life improvements based on your feedback.

We’re also building on the early response to PvE Live Events, with more capabilities planned as we move through the opening Seasons. The same is true for end-of-match rewards. What you’re seeing today is the starting point, and we have more ways to reward playing matches planned for later in the year.

As we move into upcoming Campaigns, we’ll keep a close eye on how smaller, more focused squads are landing and how long new Player Items continue to feel meaningful in your Club. Destined for Glory gives us another opportunity to build on that approach and keep the chase for new players exciting without making what you already have feel outdated too quickly.
Gallery will continue to grow through new Sets and Token Store updates, and we’re continuing to collect feedback and work through known issues as we look to enhance your experience.

And for those of you using partner sites, we’re working toward making more FUT data available through those integrations. More than 150,000 linked accounts this early tells us these tools are already becoming a meaningful part of how some players plan and manage their Clubs, and we’re excited to see where that can go next.

We’ll keep you posted as we make progress, with more to share in the weeks ahead. We’ll also be hosting a FUT specific Q&A in the Official EA SPORTS FC Discord, stay tuned for an official date and time announcement. You can also continue to share your FUT 27 feedback through the Player Feedback Portal.
The FC FUT Development Team
Welcome to the Gameplay Developer Launch Update.

First of all, the Gameplay Team is really excited to see everyone getting their hands on FC 27. Alongside your feedback, we’re also monitoring gameplay data to understand how things are playing out across the game. We can see players adapting to things like the increased emphasis on manual defending, while also trying out newer mechanics like the updated corner kicks.

For now, we’re going to keep an eye on how things develop as everyone learns the game and settles into the way FC 27 plays, while also looking into any concerns that become wider topics across the community.

We wanted to share a few things that we’ve been monitoring, but it's important to acknowledge the most important piece of feedback we got from you last year. You asked us to give you more time to learn the game, to settle in, and to enjoy the experience without title updates changing how the game feels.

We're taking that feedback to heart. We’re going to be very measured when it comes to any changes to core gameplay, looking at the wider feedback we’re hearing alongside our data and considering what’s best for FC 27 over the long term.

So, while we’re going to mention some things we're watching, it's important to note that an item appearing on this list doesn't mean that changes are coming. It simply means we’re keeping an eye on it because it’s something you’re talking about.
Fullbacks
One of the largest quantities of feedback we’ve received has been around fullbacks dropping too early and breaking the defensive line.

We know this can be frustrating when it leads to a goal, so we’ve been doing some work to better understand what’s happening and identify a potential fix if one becomes necessary. Given your feedback about giving the game time before making changes that may have a significant impact on how the game plays, we’re going to continue our investigation before making any adjustments.
Goals from Kick-off

We’ve also seen conversations about kick off goals happening more often. We’ve noticed some early movement in the data that we’re keeping an eye on to understand whether it develops into a wider trend. We’ll continue to keep a close eye on this and investigate what could be causing the increase.
Passing and Interceptions

There has been some discussion around the balance between passing and interceptions. Our design goals are to reward the manual defender for getting into passing lanes, and we feel we’re achieving that. That said, players using items with lower defensive attributes may be too effective at making the types of interceptions you’d typically expect to see from the best defenders. We'll continue to keep an eye on this, but we want to make sure manual defending is rewarded.
Shooting

Another topic that has come up is the balance between shooting types. We’ve seen feedback that low driven shots, particularly towards the near post, can be stronger than other options. One of our core philosophies is that players should be rewarded for earning a shot from a dangerous area. We’re pretty happy with the current balance between shooting and goalkeeping, but we’ll continue to monitor your feedback and our data for any potential outliers.

While we aren’t changing anything that would impact core gameplay, we are looking into several issues related to fouls. For example, we’ve seen reports of referees not giving the correct outcome following certain challenges, which the team is currently investigating.

We’ve heard the feedback that the game changes too much early in the year and are committed to not making changes too quickly. We’ll continue to monitor your feedback, continue watching your videos and reading your threads, but we won’t rush to make changes until we’re confident there’s an issue that needs to be addressed.

We’ll be hosting a Gameplay specific Q&A in the Official EA SPORTS FC Discord, stay tuned for an official date and time announcement. You can also continue to share your FC 27 through the Player Feedback Portal. Enjoy the game, and keep letting us know what you think!

releases.displayName: EA SPORTS FC™ 27 | FC 27 Launch Update Deep Dive

items.text: Hey Steam Community!

In EA SPORTS FC™ 27 we’re building on our commitment to live service support to bring you more new content, updates, and improvements across the game. This season, we’re putting additional development resource into the post-launch experience to keep your favourite modes fresh – from Football Ultimate Team™ and The Grounds to Career Mode, ongoing quality-of-life updates, and beyond.

The Launch Roadmap you see below is an early look at the headlines of what we have planned across the opening Seasons. It also reflects our commitment to giving you greater visibility into what’s ahead when you jump into the game from 18 September, and you can expect to see us sharing our plans across our various community platforms as the season progresses. We’ll be listening to your feedback too, so we can evolve the FC 27 experience with you.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/b60987441b4440b83a05308a6021c92b1f65a7ac.png"]

In this Pitch Notes, we’ll take you through what you need to know as you get ready for launch, whether you’re building your Football Ultimate Team, developing your Pro, managing your Club to glory, or playing with friends in The Grounds.

Your feedback will continue to play an important role throughout the Season. You can share your thoughts through the FC Feedback page across the Player Feedback Portal, Discord, EA Forums, and here on the Steam Forums. The Pitch Notes will provide more details on updates and changes throughout FC 27. For a deeper look at the new features in The Grounds, Football Ultimate Team, and Career, check out their respective Deep Dives.
Before we get into everything coming with launch, here are some key dates for when you can jump into EA SPORTS FC™ 27:
Web App: The EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Web App launches on 16 September at 17:00 UTC.
Companion App: The EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Companion App refresh goes live on 17 September at 17:00 UTC.
Early Access: EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Ultimate Edition players can start playing on Steam on 17 September at 23:00 UTC.
EA Play Pro: EA Play Pro members can access the full game on 17 September at 23:00 UTC.
EA Play Trial: EA Play members can access a 10-hour trial on 18 September at 04:00 UTC.
Worldwide Launch: EA SPORTS FC™ 27 launches on Steam on 24 September at 23:00 UTC.

Based on your feedback, in FC 27, we’re taking a refreshed approach to how you build and progress your Football Ultimate Team™. We want to better preserve what makes your players unique on the pitch, have every match move your Club forward, and give you more flexibility over how to upgrade your squad.
Here are the three main ideas shaping our approach.

More Choice In How You Build Your Club: There are many ways to build your squad in FUT, and we want you to have more flexibility in deciding which ones work for you. That includes a greater focus on tradeable rewards and FUT Coins. It also means better balance across the various ways you earn upgrades, including SBCs, Evolutions, and Campaign upgrades, ensuring each system offers compelling upgrades.

Preserving What Makes Players Unique: We want the players you add to your Club to have more opportunities to play a meaningful role in your squad throughout the Season. In FC 27, we’re taking a more measured approach to how Items upgrade, with fewer Campaigns, smaller Campaign squads, and more targeted upgrades to Attributes and PlayStyles. Our aim is to better preserve the individual qualities that make each player feel distinct on the pitch.

Every Game Helps Move Your Club Forward: FUT is all about building your dream squad, and the matches you play should be an important part of that journey. In FC 27, increased FUT Coin rewards and Season Points from eligible matches mean playing games can contribute more directly to your Club’s progression.
More Control Over How You Build Your Club
Tradeability & the Transfer Market
In FC 27, a significantly higher proportion of rewards across Objectives, game modes, and other areas of FUT will be tradeable.

Alongside our wider approach to Special Items, which we’ll cover later in this Pitch Notes, this is intended to give you more flexibility when using the Transfer Market, making it easier to turn the rewards you earn into opportunities to build and improve your squad throughout the Season.

With more tradeable rewards, you’ll also have more flexibility in how you choose to upgrade your squad, whether that’s bidding on Player Items, completing Evolutions, accessing the Premium Pass, or saving toward something you want to add to your Club later in the Season.
Champions Token Rewards

Tokens were introduced in FUT 26 this summer to give you more choice over the rewards you play towards. Champions Tokens return in FC 27, allowing you to choose from different reward options based on what makes the most sense for your Club.
The Champions Token Store will also feature rewards specific to Champions, including Team of the Week Players with the exclusive Red Item design, Evolutions, and vanity rewards such as Celebrations.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/49d1c881deafc234ad2798d501820c2c275dc680.png"]
TOTW Community Player
Team of the Week celebrates the players delivering standout performances across the world of football each week. In FC 27, we’re giving you a greater role in shaping who gets recognized.

During Season 1, the FC community will help to shape the selection of one player item in each of the first six Team of the Week squads. Starting 14 September, every player in the FC 27 Ratings Database is eligible to receive votes, so you can back the player you think deserves a place in the next TOTW.

A new voting period begins each Tuesday. You can vote for one player each week and change your selection at any time before voting closes each Monday at 11:59pm PT. You’ll need to log in to your EA Account to confirm your vote.
Community votes will help inform the final selection each week, with the selected player item featuring a Community Player marker in-game.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/60454ae4ef252978fb9e9248e36a7f5277cdd368.png"]
Balancing Packs and Store at Launch

As part of our broader approach to progression in EA SPORTS FC™ 27, we’re also making changes to the Store. Our intention for Store content is that it should be an optional complement to the rewards and progression available across FUT™, with playing the game remaining the cornerstone of how you build your Club.
From launch, we’re taking a more focused approach to Store content. You’ll see fewer promotional Pack offers available, alongside lower user limits on certain offers.
Combined with a series of additional changes to Store offer design, these changes are about ensuring your time on the pitch is always the most important way to build your squad.
Rarity & Pack Updates

With the removal of the distinction between Common and Rare players in FC 27, we want to make sure it remains clear what each Pack contains and what you can expect when opening them. As part of this, we’re updating how Packs are named and structured, with more consistent naming across base Packs and terms such as Mini, Small, Large, Jumbo, and Giant indicating Pack size.

While some Pack names and structures are changing as part of the Rarity refresh, our intent is for the overall Pack-opening experience to remain consistent year over year. As we outlined in our FUT Deep Dive, while Packs will no longer state a minimum number of Rare Items, the likelihood of receiving a base Player Item at OVR 82 and below is intended to remain consistent with what you would have found in similar Packs from FC 26.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/b3151397564df5e35ffe52f7f3fa6f4e8d3010ca.png"]

We’re also adjusting Quick Sell values to reflect the updated Rarity system. Player Item Quick Sell values will be more closely aligned with previous Rare Player Item values, while non-Player items will have more consistent Quick Sell values across Rarities.
Meaningful Player Items, Lasting Impact
Earning Player Items across FUT™

Squad Building Challenges, mode rewards, Evolutions, and the Transfer Market will all provide different ways to add engaging Player Items to your squad. Our goal is for these different paths to work together, giving you more choice in how you build your team and more reasons to engage with the parts of Football Ultimate Team™ you enjoy most.

In FC 27, we want every way of building your Club to feel viable and rewarding. However you choose to play, the time you put in should feel meaningful and help you build and improve your squad. By bringing the different ways you can progress closer together, our goal is to make sure you can keep playing the parts of Ultimate Team you enjoy while continuing to move your Club forward.
To support this multi-path approach and give every Item more ability to feel impactful, here is how item progression will feel different in FC 27:

Steadier Upgrade Pacing Across All Content: Our goal is for the Player Items you add to your Club, whether from SBCs, Evolutions, mode rewards, or Campaigns, to stay in your squad for longer. To enable this, we’re establishing a more gradual upgrade pacing across the year by reducing the maximum number of PlayStyles+ from five to three and reducing the attribute increases between Campaigns.

Greater Squad-Building Flexibility: To give you the freedom to fit players earned from any path into your preferred style of play, all Campaign Player Items will launch with all of their position’s Roles++ unlocked, making squad-building more flexible across different formations and playstyles.
More Focused Campaign Squads

To give Campaign Items more opportunity to feature in your squad over time, we’re changing how Campaign squads are built in EA SPORTS FC™ 27. Our goal is for each Campaign to feel more focused, with smaller squads and a tighter range of Item upgrades.

That means fewer Campaign Player Items, while the lower end of each squad will generally have a closer Attribute distribution relative to the highest-rated Items. In practice, Campaign squads will have a tighter spread of Attributes and PlayStyle boosts.

The first Campaign after Early Access, Destined for Glory, is one example of this approach and will feature 15 players in the Campaign Squad release each week. Throughout the year, there will be exceptions where broader representation makes sense for a particular football moment or Campaign, but generally speaking, Campaign Squad sizes will be smaller.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/bcd9b5fecc62d2a386b1930b717633833bc1cfd6.png"]

As previously announced, there will also be approximately five fewer Campaign weeks across FC 27. Those weeks will instead feature Series, including themed periods of content such as TOTY Warm Up and TOTS Warm Up, with no new Special Items added to Packs. The first Series of FC 27 will arrive during Season 3 in December.
Evolutions

Evolutions return in FC 27 as a core way to personalize your squad and build around the players you care about most. This year, we’re refining how Evolutions fit into your overall squad-building journey so they work in better balance with Campaign Items, SBCs, and other engagement rewards.

To align with the broader changes to Item upgrades and a steadier upgrade pacing across Ultimate Team, you can still expect to see impactful Evolutions throughout the year, just at a lower frequency and released at more intentional moments. This balanced approach ensures Campaigns, SBCs, mode rewards, and Evolutions each have a distinct, meaningful role in how you improve your squad.
Evolutions will also feature more tailored progression paths, with specific positional and Attribute requirements designed to preserve a player’s unique identity and on-pitch strengths as they grow.

To help you get a wider variety of items in your Club started on an EVO journey, we’re expanding Training Camp Evolutions. These will provide accessible entry points to boost lower-rated players, giving you more flexibility over how you upgrade your squad.
Chemistry Changes
In FC 27, we’re making a few targeted changes to Chemistry focused on ICONs, Heroes, and other boosted Chemistry Items.
ICONs will continue to receive full Chemistry when played in position and provide a +1 League link to every League. Their Nation contribution is being reduced from +2 to +1.

Heroes will also continue to receive full Chemistry when played in position, while their League contribution is being reduced from +2 to +1. Their +1 Nation contribution remains unchanged. Hall of FUT Items will follow the same Chemistry rules as Heroes.

Throughout the year, we’ll also be more selective about when Campaign Items and other Special Items receive boosted Chemistry. We want these Chemistry boosts to feel meaningful when they appear, while maintaining Chemistry and squad building as an important part of FUT as the Season progresses.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/b467a44119b01ff9758a2a68bbff41c0aeae10b9.png"]ICONs, Heroes, and Hall of FUT™
In EA SPORTS FC™ 27, we’re recalibrating how ICONs and Heroes stack up against one another, giving each tier a clearer identity and role within squad building.

ICONs represent players who built up their trophy cabinet or sustained world-class excellence across their careers, with the greatest among them helping define football history. Heroes highlight players remembered for unforgettable moments, celebrated club or league spells, and lasting impact they made on fans.
To reinforce that distinction, Base ICONs now start at 88 OVR, with refreshed Attributes and PlayStyles that reflect their status in FUT from launch.
We welcome the following new ICONs to FC 27.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/d447cb088977548a9117b63ab1b01caf3712f7c4.png"]

Hall of FUT is a new tier celebrating players whose impact in EA SPORTS FC and FUT made them unforgettable, whether through perfect links, standout performances, or lasting memories they created in your squads.

Base Hall of FUT Player Items will be available throughout EA SPORTS FC™ 27 through the Token Store, while special Campaign versions will begin appearing in Packs later in the year. Base Hall of FUT Items can also be used in Evolutions when they meet the relevant requirements.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/a708fc0a78e24055ac2db463c8e0722a92ee0c50.jpg"]

notes.title: Every Game Helps You Build Your Club

items.text: Post Match Rewards

In EA SPORTS FC™ 27, we want every match you play to contribute more directly to building your Football Ultimate Team™, whether you’re working toward your weekly rewards, have already reached them, or simply have time for a few matches.

To support that, we’re significantly increasing the FUT Coins earned after matches in Rivals, Champions, and Squad Battles. Compared to the roughly 500 to 600 FUT Coins typically earned from a match in EA SPORTS FC™ 26, Champions and Rivals will have the potential to reward several times more Coins, while Squad Battles will also see an increase.
You’ll also earn between 15 & 100 Season Points per eligible match depending on result and mode, up to 850 Season Points per day.

These changes work alongside the higher proportion of tradeable rewards in FC 27. More potential FUT Coins from playing and more tradeable Items are intended to give you greater flexibility in the Transfer Market, complete Evolutions, or save toward the next addition to your squad.

Weekly rewards will continue to provide meaningful milestones, but they’re just one of the ways you can keep progressing with your Club. Our goal is for matches beyond weekly reward thresholds to still help move your Club forward.

Based on your feedback after launch, we’ll also look for opportunities to expand post-match rewards further, including increased rewards for players in higher Divisions and additional reward types such as Tokens.
Game Modes
In EA SPORTS FC™ 27, each mode has a clearer role in how you compete, earn rewards, and build toward your next goal.
Rivals provides ongoing PvP play throughout the week
Champions provides exciting and exclusive rewards
Squad Battles offers a flexible PvE option
Live Events introduce rotating ways to play around current Campaigns and Seasons.
Division Rivals
In EA SPORTS FC™ 27, we’re creating a more noticeable difference in rewards between Divisions, giving you more to play for as you move up the Rivals ladder.
Bounties will also return and appear more frequently, giving you additional ways to earn Weekly Reward Points or accelerate your movement through the Rivals ladder.
We’re also increasing the amount of FUT Coins available through Rivals, and all Pack rewards will be tradeable at launch.

notes.title: For example, Division 1 Upgraded Rewards will include

items.text: 95,000 Coins
4x 84+ Gold Players Pack
5x 83+ Gold Players Pack
1 of 5 83+ Gold Players
Giant Gold Pack (similar to FC26 Rare Mega Pack)
TOTW Player Pack
Champions

The 15-match Champions Finals structure returns in EA SPORTS FC™ 27, alongside increased FUT Coin rewards compared to EA SPORTS FC™ 26. We’re also making changes to give you more ways to play toward qualification and your next Champions entry:
Champions Qualification Points (CQP) can now be earned through both Rivals and Squad Battles.
The Division 6 requirement for Champions qualification has been removed.
Champions rewards will include more Champions Qualification Points.

Higher Rivals Divisions will allow you to earn CQP faster, but your Division will no longer determine whether you can play toward qualification. If you earn enough CQP, you’ll be able to qualify for Champions.
Squad Battles
Squad Battles remain a flexible way to play at your own pace, complete Objectives, progress Evolutions, and earn weekly rewards without playing against other players.

In FC 27, each match will feel more rewarding through increased post-match FUT Coins and Season Points. Squad Battles will also award Champions Qualification Points, giving PvE players a new way to work toward Champions qualification.
Single Player Live Events will also sit alongside Squad Battles throughout EA SPORTS FC™ 27, giving PvE players more ways to take part in Campaign and Season themed football experiences.
Live Events

Live Events offer different ways to play outside of the regular weekly modes. In EA SPORTS FC™ 27, Online and Single Player Live Events will rotate throughout the new Season, with each experience connecting to current Campaigns or Seasons through themed squads, entry requirements, and rewards.

Tournaments, Gauntlets, and Exhibitions will return alongside new Single Player Live Events. The Ultimate Gauntlet will also return during Week 2 of Destined for Glory, beginning with two Rounds in Season 1.
New Ways to Use and Earn Items
Holographic Items
We previously introduced Holographic Items in our FC 27 FUT Deep Dive, where you can find more details on how they work. Here, we’ll take a closer look at where you can find them at launch.
Starting from Team of the Week 1, eligible Campaign, TOTW, Hero, ICON and other special Player Items available in the FUT Pack pool can also appear as Holographics:
87 OVR and below: Regular Holographic
88 OVR and above: Pristine Holographic

Eligible Holographics can appear in Store Packs and Reward Packs, with the Transfer Market providing another way to find specific Items. Packs or Player Picks that guarantee a fixed group of specific Player Items will not include Holographic versions.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/1d049247fd7ee6909d3011759ba0a777e786a0a8.jpg"]
Streamlined SBCs

As covered in the EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Football Ultimate Team™ Deep Dive, Streamlined SBCs are a new Squad Building Challenge format that lets you contribute eligible Items toward a target score across multiple submissions, rather than building a full squad around traditional SBC requirements. For a full breakdown of how the feature works, see the FC 27 FUT Deep Dive.
Streamlined SBCs will be available on console and PC at launch and are intended to release in the Companion App later in Season 1.
Every Player Item in Football Ultimate Team™ has an Item Score based on its OVR, Rarity, and Holographic status. This same scoring system is used across both Streamlined SBCs and Gallery.

Each OVR has a base score, which can then be increased by Rarity and Holographic bonuses. These bonuses stack together, so Campaign and Holographic Items can contribute more toward a Streamlined SBC target.
For example, a Holographic TOTW Item receives both its TOTW Rarity bonus and its Holographic bonus.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/cc47deadc7a5e33911164b6b0a5b7764dc2efb8b.png"]
We’ll continue monitoring Item Scores throughout EA SPORTS FC™ 27. If adjustments are needed based on player feedback or live data, we’ll provide significant advance notice before making any changes.
Gallery

Gallery gives you a meaningful, low pressure way to interact with the Items in your Club throughout your FUT journey. You can build around the Clubs, Leagues, Rarities, and football stories you care about, improve Sets over time, and earn rewards at your own pace.

As you earn Player Items throughout FC 27, they can contribute to Gallery Sets and remain part of your Gallery history even after they leave your Club. That means an Item you earn today can still become relevant to a Set introduced later on.
Each Set rewards you with Club Customisation including Club-specific Crests and Kits, while higher Grades award Gallery Tokens.
For a full breakdown of how Gallery works, including Sets, Grades, and Tags, see the EA SPORTS FC™ 27 FUT™ Deep Dive.
Gallery Token Store

Gallery Tokens can be redeemed for rewards inspired by fandom and Club identity. At launch, Base Hall of FUT Player Items will be among the featured rewards, giving you a way to earn these specific Base versions throughout EA SPORTS FC™ 27.
The Token Store will evolve throughout EA SPORTS FC™ 27 with new Kits, Crests, Holographic rewards, and more.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/0f1ff63e4b913eb25fb2e1d2dd144d61332c7a4c.png"]Gallery Level
Your progress across Gallery Sets also contributes to your overall Gallery Level, with larger rewards at key milestones:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/cd3c2de7c68555e3d03d0adb432bdac9cd858029.png"]
New Gallery Sets

More than 100 Sets will be available at launch, spanning major men’s and women’s leagues and clubs, alongside Rarity Sets such as Squad Foundations and Team of the Week. A Starter Set will also introduce you to the feature. Gallery Set releases remain live for the duration of the game.
New Sets will arrive at certain moments throughout FC 27, but not every week or alongside every Campaign.

When a new Set arrives, eligible Items already recorded in your Gallery history can count towards it, even if they are no longer in your Club. An Item obtained today could become relevant to a new Gallery Set months later.

The first post-launch Gallery Set arrives at Worldwide Launch with the Season 1 (Combined Rarities) Set, bringing together Ones to Watch, Destined for Glory, and Future Stars Player Items to collect and showcase.
Season 1: Ones to Watch & Launch Content
Now let’s take a look at some upcoming Football Ultimate Team™ Campaigns & Seasons.
Early Access
Your Ultimate or Ultimate+ Edition pre-order gives you early access to EA SPORTS FC™ 27 from 18 September, one week before worldwide launch.
During Early Access, you’ll be able to get started with the following:
Team of the Week 1 & 2
Ones to Watch Themed Player SBCs
Challenge and Upgrade SBCs
Evolutions
Squad Foundations
Opportunities to Earn Season Points
Season 1 marks the return of the fan-favourite Ones to Watch, back bigger than ever to celebrate the summer transfers set to shape the new football season.
Earn Ones to Watch Player Items through the Season Pass, with select players also available through SBCs and Objectives from Early Access.

In EA SPORTS FC™ 27, each Season will have a distinct theme connecting its Campaigns through one wider journey. Season 1 brings together Ones to Watch, Destined for Glory, and Future Stars, all centred on players ready to make their mark on the football season ahead. Look out for future Seasons inspired by nostalgia, football heritage and beloved cult football eras.
Season 1: Ones to Watch will be live from Thursday, 17 September 2026 to Thursday, 22 October 2026.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/fa71446974a61c2da690c05429c567be76a930b9.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/175cc8a824f0f294eee0de68b4954784c32e294c.png"]
Ones to Watch Player Upgrades

Ones to Watch Player Items rated 83 OVR or higher retain their Base Item Attributes, while those below are boosted to 83. Every Ones to Watch Item is also guaranteed at least 60 Pace and have all their Role++ in Position.

Ones to Watch Items remain eligible for upgrades throughout the football season. They receive +1 OVR for each Team of the Week, Star Performer or Player of the Month inclusion, plus a one-time +1 OVR if their club wins three of its next six domestic league matches after 18 September.
Ones We Watched - Single Player Live Events

Season 1 begins with a Single Player Live Event series celebrating Ones to Watch from FUT 18, FUT 19, and FUT 20. Choose your difficulty for the opening stage and play a collection of different Clubs across world football.

Then, face progressively higher OVR Ones We Watched inspired AI squads and more demanding squad-building requirements as you advance. Retro Cosmetic Evolutions inspired by those years will also be available through the Season Ladder and Evolution Store.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/3dc00f8147f0159a3129dccd179e7cbf91f9dc99.png"]
Destined for Glory

On 25 September, Destined for Glory will spotlight players that you have voted to make a major impact this football season, shaped by your votes in EA SPORTS FC™ 26 Football Ultimate Team™ and the EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Ratings Database.

Led by EA SPORTS FC™ 27 cover star Kylian Mbappé, who received the most community votes, the first Destined for Glory Player Items also feature new Chelsea signing Morgan Rogers, new Tottenham Hotspur signing Matheus Fernandes, along with attackers Alexander Isak and Bryan Mbeumo.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/e287b92291aae28b1298a705f7b70636ee3c51f0.png"]

Destined for Glory Player Items can earn upgrades throughout the entire football season starting from September 18, based on real-world performances in their domestic league, with milestones determined by the player’s position.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/342d38f4a23e57b75236f81725561de4422a1467.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/4568f317f1caa2ec1b8e5f069370ce44808f7244.png"]

Available on PlayStation®5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch™ 2, and PC, The Grounds is the new home of Clubs in EA SPORTS FC™ 27. League and Playoff matches and Rush return alongside new ways for you and your Clubmates to compete. However you choose to play, your time in The Grounds helps develop your Pro.

Starting in Early Access and continuing through Worldwide Launch, the first Club Tournament will be a Classic Stadium 11v11 Event, bringing new 11v11 competition to The Grounds with its own House Rules, entry requirements, Objectives, and rewards.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/07cf717506ee5bc88bc01d9ca7d68382aca43350.png"]
Archetypes remain at the heart of how you build and master your Pro, with more freedom to experiment with different builds throughout EA SPORTS FC™ 27.
No matter where you play, on the streets or in a stadium, you will earn AXP and Grounds Coins. Limited time experiences like Club Tournaments and Playoffs will offer greater rewards.
Objectives provide another path to progress, with Cosmetic Items, AXP Consumables and Grounds Coins among the rewards you can earn.

Amps will refresh regularly, giving you new ways to experiment with how your Pro plays. Want to try a boost to Long Shots? A Standard Amp lets you test it for a few games without changing your whole build.

You’ll also discover player-themed Signature Amps inspired by some of football’s biggest stars, combining Attributes, PlayStyles, and Signature Perks that let you bring elements of their game to your Pro for a limited number of matches.
Found something you like? Resetting your build doesn’t cost Grounds Coins, giving you the freedom to keep experimenting.
At launch, Amps will not provide PlayStyle+, keeping their focus on finding new ways to play while preserving gameplay balance.
Season 1 Grounds Content
The Grounds Live Events
Throughout the new year, limited time Live Events will transform The Grounds through new ways to play and exclusive rewards inspired by football's biggest moments.
European Nights
Season 1 introduces European Nights, bringing the brightest lights of the UEFA Champions League to The Grounds. The world will remain at dusk to capture the atmosphere of Matchdays 2 and 3.

Your journey starts in the Districts. Jump into small-sided Live Events and earn your way into the European Nights 11v11 Stadium Club Tournament to compete with your Clubmates and earn bigger rewards.
Along the way, earn UEFA Champions League Player-Themed Amps inspired by champions including Zidane, Maldini and Bale, alongside exclusive Emotes, Club Kits and more.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/5edc3adf37f7dad7da2c4dd6fc580a6cd080579f.png"]
Screaming Grounds

As Halloween approaches, darkness takes over with Screaming Grounds. Take aim at pumpkin targets, jump into Halloween-themed Live Events, and flaunt fantastical Cosmetic Items like superhero-esque costumes.
The Grounds Stores
Check out The Grounds Stores for frequently updated streetwear inspired by moments across football and EA SPORTS FC™, including seasonal themes and collaborations with brands and clubs.
Boutique Montclair, Tienda Zeiza and Parkside Store will feature rotating fashion drops influenced by each District’s identity, streetwear, music and local culture.

For FC 27, Career Mode continues to expand with new ways to play throughout the Season. Manager Live returns with a fresh set of Challenges at launch, alongside new Community Driven Challenges, while Season 1 will also bring a new selection of ICONs to unlock and use across Career Mode.
Manager Live
We’re kicking off FC 27 with a varied line-up of Manager Live Challenges, designed to offer different Objectives, varying time commitments, and ways to approach your Career.

Our Starter Challenges provide an accessible way to jump straight into Manager Live, built around familiar Career Mode experiences such as navigating the transfer market, building early-Season momentum, and chasing some of football’s biggest milestones.

notes.title: Here are a few of the Challenges waiting for you

items.text: Transfer Savvy: set your Season off with a shrewd profit in the opening transfer window.
Winning Start: go undefeated in the opening weeks of the new League Season, while winning at least three matches along the way.
Top at Christmas: put yourself at the top of the tree by leading your league when Christmas arrives.
Rio's Rising: make 2026/27 the season Rio Ngumoha cements his status as a superstar at Anfield.

That’s only some of the Challenges at the starting point. Throughout FC 27, Manager Live will continue to evolve with new Challenges inspired by the football season, giving you new scenarios and stories to take on as the year unfolds.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46226104/185dbf289338e38675fef67f775dd78f475fef25.png"]Creator Challenges
One of the biggest additions to Manager Live in FC 27 is the ability to create your own Challenges and share them with friends.

These Challenges give us another way to celebrate how you play Career Mode, from recreating stories that players are already talking about to exploring some of the more unexpected ideas that could only happen in a Career save.
We also aim to feature Challenges created by Creators from our Career Community shortly after launch.
Keep an eye on Manager Live throughout the new Season for new Community Driven Challenges and more opportunities to put your own spin on the football world.
ICONs in Player Career & Manager Career
ICONs will once again be part of the Career Mode experience in FC 27, with new players becoming available to unlock throughout the Seasons.
Season 1 will feature a selection of some of football’s most memorable names, including: Kaká, Antonio Di Natale, Alessandro Del Piero, Raúl, Robin van Persie.

Thanks for taking the time to read through the Pitch Notes here on Steam. We hope this has given you a better idea of what to expect as we head into the launch of EA SPORTS FC™ 27 and some of what’s to come throughout the Season.

As always, we’ll continue to listen to your feedback as you get hands-on with the game and share more details on updates and changes when there’s more to discuss. Stay tuned for more FC 27 Pitch Notes, including our Launch Rewards Pitch Notes coming later this week, and join the conversation in the EA SPORTS FC™ Discord.
We look forward to seeing you on the pitch.
The EA SPORTS FC™ Team

releases.displayName: EA SPORTS FC™ 27 | Closed Beta Feedback Update

items.text: [p align="start"]During the EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Closed Beta, we heard your feedback across the game through the EA Closed Beta Forums, the FC 27 Closed Beta Player Feedback Portal, and Discord. We’ve been reviewing that feedback to better understand your experience and the topics that mattered most to you.

[p align="start"]In this Pitch Notes, we’ll cover improvements driven by your feedback across areas including physical play, Team Press, Lengthy players, and more. We’ll also provide more context on some of the topics you’ve raised and share our approach to gameplay updates during the launch period.

[p align="start"]We’ve been closely following player conversations and know there’s feedback about significant gameplay balance changes being made after launch. For EA SPORTS FC™ 27, we want to take a measured approach and do not plan on making significant gameplay balance changes in our early Title Updates.

[p align="start"]How the game is played and understood can evolve quickly during the opening weeks as players learn new mechanics, discover different ways to play, and build squads. Because of that, we don’t want to react quickly to early trends with significant balance changes. Instead, we’ll give the gameplay experience time to settle so we can better understand how the game develops and whether adjustments are needed.

[p align="start"]Our intention is to preserve the gameplay experience we’ve built for launch and give players time to learn and adapt to it. We’ll continue listening closely to your feedback throughout that period, which you can share through the FC Feedback Hub.

[p align="start"]We’ll still look to address bugs, unintended behaviours, and other issues that are significantly impacting the gameplay experience. In some cases, addressing these issues may have an impact on the balance of related gameplay systems. For example, addressing an unintended Goalkeeper behaviour could affect the balance between shooting and Goalkeeping more broadly. When fixes like these are needed, we’ll aim to make them as targeted as possible to address the specific issue while limiting their impact on the wider gameplay experience.

[p align="start"]Physical play and the Bruiser PlayStyle have been big topics coming out of the EA SPORTS FC™ 27 Closed Beta. We still want physical play to be a viable way to win the ball while defending, but we’ve made some changes to make Shoulder Challenges more consistent and address some unintended ways they could’ve been used.
[p align="start"]Shoulder Challenges should be most effective when the defender gets side-by-side with the ball carrier rather than attempting a challenge from behind.

[p align="start"]One behaviour we wanted to address was repeatedly pressing Shoulder Challenge while chasing an opponent until a challenge eventually triggered. Now, repeatedly pressing Shoulder Challenge in quick succession will cause the defender to stick out an arm and lose speed, making it more difficult to chase down an opponent by repeatedly using the input.

[p align="start"]When you get into the right position and time the challenge properly, physical defending remains effective. Strength continues to play an important role, with the Bruiser PlayStyle providing an additional benefit. We’ve also slightly reduced the additional benefit provided by Bruiser+.
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]Team Press is intended to be a way to apply pressure higher up the pitch, but we found it was also too effective when used close to your own goal. In those situations, AI teammates could automatically close down opponents and take too much of the defensive responsibility away from the user.

[p align="start"]To address this, Team Press will now have no effect while the ball is in your defensive third. This directly addresses one of the most common ways Team Press could be used to automatically pressure attackers close to goal, requiring the defending player to take more responsibility for applying pressure in these situations.

[p align="start"]When Team Press is used further up the pitch, defenders can still step towards their marked players, but will be less effective at applying pressure than midfielders and forwards. This also comes with a trade-off: as defenders move closer to their marked players, they can become more susceptible to passes played in behind the defensive line.

[p align="start"]We also heard feedback that defensive lines could sit higher than expected, even when using a lower Defensive Depth. We’ve made adjustments so that lower depth settings are more clearly reflected in how your defensive line positions itself, with defenders retreating sooner and maintaining a more conservative position to leave less space in behind. Your defensive line will still adjust to what’s happening on the pitch, so setting a low depth doesn’t mean your defenders will stay deep in every situation.

[p align="start"]Based on your feedback during the Closed Beta, we’ve looked at AcceleRATE itself as well as some of the other mechanics that were contributing to Lengthy players being particularly effective.

[p align="start"]As previously announced in the FC 27 Gameplay Deep Dive, Triggered Runs will now have a limited distance. You’ll need to trigger another run if you want the player to continue their movement. This requires more active input when managing longer runs and also reduces some of the benefits Lengthy players could gain over extended distances.
[p align="start"]We’ve also made a couple of other changes to further address the effectiveness of Lengthy players.

[p align="start"]We’ve slightly reduced the impact of AcceleRATE profiles on a player’s running performance, bringing Explosive, Controlled, and Lengthy players a little closer together. This places greater emphasis on a player’s Acceleration and Sprint Speed Attributes.

[p align="start"]We’ve also adjusted the height threshold for female players to be eligible for the Lengthy AcceleRATE profile. In FC 27, female players will need to be at least 5’8” (172 cm) to be eligible for Lengthy.

[p align="start"]Together, we believe these changes provide a better balance between the different AcceleRATE profiles, while allowing each to remain useful depending on your players and your preferred style of play.

[p align="start"]We heard your feedback that Player Lock could be particularly effective with very little downside for an advanced mechanic. Based on that feedback, we’ve made some changes to introduce more of a risk-reward balance when using Player Lock.

[p align="start"]When you Player Lock away from the ball carrier, the ball carrier will no longer automatically dribble around or avoid defenders. Instead, they’ll continue moving in the direction they were already travelling.

[p align="start"]This gives the defending player a clearer opportunity to recognise the situation and apply pressure to the ball carrier, while requiring the attacking player to be more aware of what’s happening on the ball while controlling another player.
[p align="start"]We’ve also slightly increased the error in passes made by the CPU-controlled ball carrier during Player Lock, further adding to the risk-reward balance of using the feature.
[p align="start"]We want Player Lock to continue providing opportunities to create manual movement off the ball, while placing more responsibility on the player using it.
[p align="start"]As previously announced in the Gameplay Deep Dive, Dinked Passes are fully manual in EA SPORTS FC™ 27.

[p align="start"]Previously, Ground Pass and Through Pass could trigger different versions of the Dinked Pass, one toward a teammate and one into space. With Dinked Passes now being manual, where the ball goes will instead be determined by where you aim.

[p align="start"]During the Closed Beta, we also saw that Dinked Passes could be triggered accidentally when pressing Ground Pass multiple times. To address this, Dinked Passes can no longer be performed using the Ground Pass input. Double-tapping or repeatedly pressing Ground Pass will result in a regular Ground Pass.
[p align="start"]To perform a Dinked Pass, double tap Through Pass and manually aim where you want the ball to go.
[p align="start"]We’ve seen questions from the community about how the new Attacking Spatial Awareness system works alongside Player Roles.

[p align="start"]Player Roles continue to determine the types of runs a player can make based on their position and Role. For example, an Inside Forward can look to make runs into the space between the centre back and fullback, while a Winger will consider runs that better reflect their wider positioning.

[p align="start"]Role Familiarity then influences the urgency with which a player makes those available runs. Players with greater familiarity in a Role, including Role+ and Role++, will show more urgency when making those movements.
[p align="start"]Attacking Spatial Awareness doesn’t replace Player Roles. Instead, the two systems work together to influence a player’s attacking movement.

notes.title: Corner Kicks: What’s New in FC 27?

items.text: [p align="start"]We’ve seen questions around what is actually different about Corner Kicks in FC 27 since you could already control a player in the box in FC 26.

[p align="start"]While FC 26 gave you the ability to manually control a player in the box, the main difference with corners in FC 27 is the amount of assistance you get when manually positioning your player.

[p align="start"]EA SPORTS FC™ 27 gives you free movement and no longer moves your player toward the expected landing position of the ball. It’s now down to you to read the trajectory, get into the right position and time the run.

[p align="start"]The player you’re controlling matters too, as height and jumping ability can change where and when you want to attack the ball. A taller player with strong jumping, for example, may be able to meet the ball earlier in its trajectory. A player’s physical momentum also matters, so it’s not only about getting to the right spot, it’s also about how and when you arrive there.

[p align="start"]You can also use Shielding to help hold a good position once you’ve found it, or use the new Avoidance mechanic to slip past opponents and try to beat them to the best spot to attack the ball.

[p align="start"]Based on the feedback from the FC 27 Closed Beta, we’re making several refinements to CPU AI in Authentic Gameplay. In line with our approach to early gameplay updates, these changes are focused on targeted adjustments rather than significantly changing the overall balance of the gameplay experience.
[p align="start"]These adjustments include, but are not limited to, the following areas:
Difficulty Calibration: Tuning difficulty progression to create clearer differences between Professional, World Class, and Legendary difficulties.
Tactical Adjustments: The thresholds for certain CPU Sliders, such as Sliding Tackle Frequency, are being recalibrated for more dynamic and realistic tactical behavior.

AI Behavior: We are implementing several changes to improve how the CPU AI builds attacks, approaches 1v1 finishing opportunities, and defends against specific offensive maneuvers such as through passes and triggered runs in certain situations.
[p align="start"]We appreciate the detailed feedback you shared throughout the Closed Beta and will continue refining Authentic Gameplay ahead of launch.
